library_preparation_preflight.summary: This is a self-contained javax.activation (JAF 1.1) implementation. Its only declared dependencies (geronimo-osgi-locator, org.osgi.core, org.osgi.compendium) are provided-scope and are only needed when it runs as an OSGi bundle. It needs no services, containers or properties. A JVM smoke test of MailcapCommandMap, MimetypesFileTypeMap and DataHandler passed with only the artifact on the classpath.
risks: The JAR contains copies of org.apache.geronimo.osgi.locator.ProviderLocator and the org.apache.geronimo.specs.activation.Activator classes, which use org.osgi.* types that are not on the test classpath. Tests should not touch Activator or ProviderLocator.init(BundleContext), or they will fail with NoClassDefFoundError. Normal paths through MailcapCommandMap never trigger those OSGi types: ProviderLocator.loadClass falls back to the ClassLoader and Class.forName.

The reflective paths that need metadata: MailcapCommandMap loads content handlers from x-java-content-handler entries with Class.forName/newInstance. It also reads META-INF/mailcap, META-INF/mailcap.default and META-INF/mime.types, and MimetypesFileTypeMap reads the bundled META-INF/mimetypes.default. Tests should register a test-defined DataContentHandler through addMailcap or a test-resource META-INF/mailcap to cover these.

ActivationDataFlavor and DataContentHandler use java.awt.datatransfer.DataFlavor from the java.datatransfer module. Check that Native Image builds this cleanly, and keep tests away from wider AWT/GUI classes.

The JDK no longer includes javax.activation (removed in JDK 11), so there is no split-package conflict on JDK 25. Do not add jakarta.activation or javax.activation-api to the test classpath, because they would duplicate these classes.
